content: Vaccenic acid is a type of trans fat that is naturally present in the fat of ruminant animals and in dairy products. Its chemical name, according to IUPAC nomenclature, is trans-7-octadecenoic acid, and it is commonly referred to in lipid shorthand as 18:1 trans-11. The name vaccenic is derived from the Latin word vacca, meaning cow. This fatty acid was first identified in 1928 in animal fats and butter. It is the predominant trans fatty acid isomer found in milk fat. In mammals, vaccenic acid is metabolized into rumenic acid, a conjugated linoleic acid that exhibits anticancer properties. The stereoisomer of vaccenic acid, known as cis-vaccenic acid, is an Omega-7 fatty acid that is found in sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides) oil. Its IUPAC name is cis-7-octadecenoic acid, and its lipid shorthand name is 18:1 cis-11. In the April 2001 issue of The Journal of Investigative Dermatology, Shinichiro Haze and colleagues published an article titled 2-Nonenal, Newly Found in Human Body Odor Tends to Increase with Aging. This study proposed that Omega-7 unsaturated fatty acids, such as palmitoleic acid and vaccenic acid, which are present on the surface of the skin, may contribute to the phenomenon commonly referred to as old person smell.
